## Big Question {.role-slide}

How should an annotation model connect recorded responses to the linguistic quantity they are intended to measure?

## Data {.role-slide}

An annotator sees a prompt, uses an interface, selects a response, and may receive a conditional follow up question.

## Challenge {.role-slide}

The recorded response is not the linguistic property itself.

Aggregation can remove the evidence needed to distinguish item structure from response behavior.

## This Module {.role-slide .compact}

1. Separate annotations from their target construct.
2. Write the data-generating process before the likelihood.
3. Translate each random step into one probability factor.
4. Add annotator effects and gated responses.
5. Test the complete procedure through parameter recovery.
6. Fit a narrow measurement model for UDS natural parts judgments.

## Annotations as measurements {.section-slide}

What is observed and what is inferred

## Question {.role-slide}

What does a seven point event likelihood judgment directly measure?

## Answer {.role-slide}

It directly measures a response produced by a prompt, scale, interface, and annotator.

The intended semantic property is unobserved.

## Method {.role-slide}

Let $Y_{ij}$ be annotator $j$'s recorded response to item $i$.

Let $\theta_i$ be the item property that the response is intended to inform.

## Answer {.role-slide}

A [measurement model](https://bruno.nicenboim.me/bayescogsci/ch-custom.html) describes

$$p(Y_{ij}\mid\theta_i,\text{annotator }j,\text{instrument}).$$

The response and the latent item property receive different symbols.

::: {.notes}
[Sources]

Nicenboim, Schad, and Vasishth, Custom Models: https://bruno.nicenboim.me/bayescogsci/ch-custom.html
:::

## Data {.role-slide}

| item | j1 | j2 | j3 | j4 | mean |
|:--|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| A | 4 | 4 | 4 | 4 | 4 |
| B | 1 | 2 | 6 | 7 | 4 |

## Surprising Fact {.role-slide}

The item means are identical, but the response patterns provide different evidence about agreement and scale use.

## Important Point #1 {.role-slide}

Aggregation removes annotator identities, response shape, and often the response count.

The item mean cannot reconstruct those features.

## Question {.role-slide}

Does reliable agreement establish that an annotation measures the intended construct?

## Answer {.role-slide}

No. Reliability concerns consistency. Validity concerns whether the measurement supports the intended interpretation.

## Method {.role-slide .compact}

Before writing a likelihood, state the response support, the interpretation of endpoints, the display rules for follow up questions, the confidence format, and the repeated item and annotator units.

## Upshot {.role-slide}

Raw annotations preserve evidence that an aggregate may discard. The model must begin from the instrument that generated those annotations.

<span class="source">White et al. 2020</span>

::: {.notes}
[Sources]

White et al., The Universal Decompositional Semantics Dataset and Decomp Toolkit: https://aclanthology.org/2020.lrec-1.699/
:::

## From process to probability {.section-slide}

Order the random steps, then write the joint model

## Question {.role-slide}

How could a latent sentence value, response noise, and ordered thresholds produce one recorded category?

## Answer {.role-slide}

A [data-generating process](https://bruno.nicenboim.me/bayescogsci/ch-workflow.html) is an ordered account of random choices and deterministic mappings that could produce an observation.

::: {.notes}
[Sources]

Nicenboim, Schad, and Vasishth, Bayesian Workflow: https://bruno.nicenboim.me/bayescogsci/ch-workflow.html
:::

## Implementation {.role-slide}

1. Give sentence $i$ an unobserved value $\theta_i$.
2. Generate a trial response $Z_{ij}$ around that value.
3. Map $Z_{ij}$ to the recorded category $Y_{ij}$ using ordered thresholds.

## Method {.role-slide}

$$Z_{ij}=\theta_i+\varepsilon_{ij},\qquad \varepsilon_{ij}\sim\operatorname{Logistic}(0,1).$$

Then $Y_{ij}=k$ when $c_{k-1}<Z_{ij}\leq c_k$.

## Question {.role-slide}

Let $\theta_i=.8$, $\varepsilon_{ij}=-.2$, and thresholds $-1$, $0$, and $1$.

Which response category is recorded?

## Answer {.role-slide}

$Z_{ij}=.6$, which lies between 0 and 1.

The recorded category is 3.

## Important Point #1 {.role-slide}

The numeral 3 is not treated as a direct observation of $\theta_i$.

It records the threshold interval containing one latent trial response.

## Important Point #2 {.role-slide}

Every recorded variable must appear in the process or be explicitly excluded from the model's scope.

Every latent variable must affect an observation in an identifiable way.

## Question {.role-slide}

How does the verbal process become a probability model that can be fitted?

## Answer {.role-slide}

A [joint probability model](https://bruno.nicenboim.me/bayescogsci/ch-custom.html) assigns one probability factor to every random step in the data-generating process.

::: {.notes}
[Sources]

Nicenboim, Schad, and Vasishth, Custom Models: https://bruno.nicenboim.me/bayescogsci/ch-custom.html
:::

## Method {.role-slide}

For binary annotations with item log odds $\theta_i$,

$$Y_{ij}\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(\operatorname{logit}^{-1}(\theta_i)).$$

## Output {.role-slide}

$$p(\mathbf y,\boldsymbol\theta\mid\mu_\theta,\tau_\theta)=
\prod_i p(\theta_i\mid\mu_\theta,\tau_\theta)
\prod_{(i,j)\in\mathcal O}p(y_{ij}\mid\theta_i).$$

## Interpretation {.role-slide}

Repeated appearances of $\theta_i$ make responses to item $i$ share one item quantity.

The conditional arguments, not multiplication order, state dependencies.

## Challenge {.role-slide}

An item mean computed from the raw responses is not a second independent observation.

Adding a likelihood for both would count the same responses twice.

## Upshot {.role-slide}

Trace every probability factor to one random step and one recorded event. This prevents hidden assumptions and duplicated evidence.

## Annotator variation {.section-slide}

Stable response location across items

## Question {.role-slide}

How can a model represent an annotator who tends to affirm more often across all items?

## Answer {.role-slide}

Add the [annotator random intercept introduced earlier](../../regression-models/random-intercepts.html) without changing the item quantity.

## Method {.role-slide}

$$\operatorname{logit}(\pi_{ij})=\theta_i+a_j$$

$$a_j\sim\operatorname{Normal}(0,\sigma_a^2).$$

## Interpretation {.role-slide}

A positive $a_j$ raises affirmative log odds for every item seen by annotator $j$.

It is stable response location, not trial noise.

## Question {.role-slide}

If $\theta_i=0$, what probabilities correspond to annotator effects $a_1=1$ and $a_2=-1$?

## Answer {.role-slide}

$$\operatorname{logit}^{-1}(1)=.73$$

$$\operatorname{logit}^{-1}(-1)=.27$$

## Challenge {.role-slide}

Adding a constant to every item value and subtracting it from every annotator value leaves all predicted probabilities unchanged.

## Answer {.role-slide}

Fix the coordinate system by centering one effect population at zero.

The resulting intercept and deviations then have a defined location.

## Important Point #1 {.role-slide}

A random intercept represents stable location differences only.

Differences in discrimination, thresholds, or response consistency require separate model components.

## Upshot {.role-slide}

Annotator and item effects can be separated only when their coordinate system is identified and the observation design connects annotators through shared items.

## Gated annotations {.section-slide}

Model the question that was actually displayed

## Data {.role-slide}

An annotation protocol first asks whether an event has a property.

Only a yes response reveals the follow up scale for degree.

## Challenge {.role-slide}

A blank follow up after a no response is generated by the protocol.

It is not a zero and not a failed measurement of a displayed question.

## Question {.role-slide}

How should the gate and conditional follow up contribute to the joint model?

## Answer {.role-slide}

$$
p(g_{ij},y_{ij}^{\mathrm{obs}})=
\begin{cases}
\pi_{ij}f_Y(y_{ij}\mid\phi_{ij}),&g_{ij}=1,\\
1-\pi_{ij},&g_{ij}=0.
\end{cases}
$$

## Question {.role-slide}

The affirmative gate probability is .70. Conditional on affirmation, category 6 has probability .25.

What is their joint contribution?

## Answer {.role-slide}

$$.70\times.25=.175.$$

A negative gate contributes only $1-.70=.30$.

## Important Point #1 {.role-slide}

The follow up model describes responses conditional on the gate being affirmative.

It does not describe the complete item population without the gate model.

## Important Point #2 {.role-slide}

Shared item and annotator quantities may connect the gate and follow up.

That dependence must appear in the joint model rather than in an after the fact correlation.

## Upshot {.role-slide}

A gated model follows the instrument. It assigns no follow up value to a trial on which the follow up question was never asked.

## Parameter recovery {.section-slide}

Can the planned procedure recover what generated the data?

## Challenge {.role-slide}

A model can fit without warnings even when several parameter combinations produce nearly identical response distributions.

## Answer {.role-slide}

[Parameter recovery](https://mc-stan.org/learn-stan/case-studies/rasch_and_2pl.html) tests the complete inference procedure on simulated data with known generating values.

::: {.notes}
[Sources]

Stan case study, Rasch and two parameter logistic models: https://mc-stan.org/learn-stan/case-studies/rasch_and_2pl.html
:::

## Implementation {.role-slide}

1. Choose generating values and a sample design.
2. Simulate latent quantities and recorded responses.
3. Fit the planned model.
4. Compare fitted summaries with generating values.

## Important Point #1 {.role-slide}

Fitting must occur in every replicate.

Inspecting simulated responses tests the generator, not the estimator and fitting procedure.

## Output {.role-slide}

Across replicates, inspect bias, absolute error, interval coverage, rank correlation, convergence diagnostics, and computational failures.

## Important Point #2 {.role-slide}

Test difficult regions, including rare gates, sparse annotators, extreme probabilities, and weakly connected item by annotator designs.

## Interpretation {.role-slide}

Failed recovery blocks precise interpretation under the model's own assumptions.

Successful recovery does not establish that real annotators follow the assumed process.

## Upshot {.role-slide}

Recovery supports a conditional claim: the procedure recovered a named quantity over a stated range under a stated design and generator.

## UDS natural parts judgments {.section-slide}

A narrow measurement model for binary annotations

## Question {.role-slide}

What can the released yes and no responses support about whether predicate instances describe situations with natural parts?

## Data {.role-slide}

*The broker called back shortly after I spoke to you.*

All three annotators answered no.

## Data {.role-slide}

*Around what time they eat each of their meals.*

All three annotators answered yes.

<span class="source">Gantt, Glass, and White 2022</span>

::: {.notes}
[Sources]

Gantt, Glass, and White, Decomposing and recomposing event structure: https://aclanthology.org/2022.tacl-1.2/
:::

## Important Point #1 {.role-slide}

These are responses to predicate instances in context.

They are not direct observations of event structure or context free lexical properties.

## Goal {.role-slide}

Estimate the conditional probability of yes for one predicate instance when the annotator random intercept is zero.

The raw binary response is the only likelihood input.

## Data {.role-slide}

| quantity | count |
|:--|--:|
| predicate instances | 1,000 |
| annotators | 12 |
| raw responses | 2,955 |
| yes responses | 659 |

<span class="source">Pinned UDS teaching extract</span>

::: {.notes}
[Sources]

Course dataset audit and measurement model: ../../custom-models/uds-measurement-model.html

Official decomp package: https://decomp.io/
:::

## Challenge {.role-slide}

Most items have three responses, and annotator yes rates vary from about .02 to .43.

Raw item proportions ignore uncertainty and annotator composition.

## Method {.role-slide}

$$Y_{ij}\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(\pi_{ij})$$

$$\operatorname{logit}(\pi_{ij})=\alpha+u_i+a_j.$$

## Interpretation {.role-slide}

$u_i$ is an item deviation. $a_j$ is an annotator location deviation.

Both sets are centered at zero to identify $\alpha$.

## Important Point #2 {.role-slide}

$\operatorname{logit}^{-1}(\alpha+u_i)$ is conditional on an annotator effect of zero.

It is not the marginal probability averaged over annotators.

## Implementation {.role-slide}

Before fitting UDS responses, use the exact item by annotator incidence pattern to test recovery of $\alpha$, both scale parameters, item effects, annotator effects, and item probabilities.

## Result #1 {.role-slide}

Across 12 recovery fits, median item effect correlation is .662 and median annotator effect correlation is .958.

There are no divergent transitions.

<span class="source">Course recovery study</span>

::: {.notes}
[Sources]

Course UDS measurement model and recovery results: ../../custom-models/uds-measurement-model.html
:::

## Interpretation {.role-slide}

The design supports a regularized item ordering for this teaching analysis.

Three responses do not make each item propensity precise.

## Result #2 {.role-slide}

The fitted item scale has posterior median 2.077.

The fitted annotator scale has posterior median 2.050.

<span class="source">Course fit to released UDS responses</span>

::: {.notes}
[Sources]

Course UDS measurement model results: ../../custom-models/uds-measurement-model.html
:::

## Interpretation {.role-slide}

Predicate instances vary substantially in natural parts responses.

Annotators also show substantial stable location differences after item variation is represented.

## Result #3 {.role-slide}

The posterior median conditional probability is .009 for *called* and .800 for *eat*.

Their raw proportions are 0 and 1.

<span class="source">Course fit to released UDS responses</span>

::: {.notes}
[Sources]

Course UDS measurement model results: ../../custom-models/uds-measurement-model.html
:::

## Interpretation {.role-slide}

Partial pooling moves the estimates away from the raw endpoints while accounting for the annotators who saw each item.

## Result #4 {.role-slide}

[Posterior predictive simulations](../../statistical-inference/posterior-predictive-checks.html) reproduce the overall yes rate and the proportion of items containing both yes and no responses.

<span class="source">Course posterior predictive checks</span>

::: {.notes}
[Sources]

Course UDS measurement model results: ../../custom-models/uds-measurement-model.html
:::

## Result #5 {.role-slide}

Posterior median item probabilities correlate .818 with the released normalized values by Spearman correlation.

The released values were not used during fitting.

<span class="source">Course comparison with UDS release</span>

::: {.notes}
[Sources]

Course UDS measurement model results: ../../custom-models/uds-measurement-model.html
:::

## Important Point #3 {.role-slide}

The model does not estimate part similarity, duration, dynamicity, confidence, or the relation between annotation branches.

Each addition requires its own response model and recovery study.

## Upshot {.role-slide}

The binary item by annotator model supports one narrow measurement of natural parts responses while preserving the limits imposed by the released annotation design.

## Conclusion {.section-slide}

What custom model design requires

## Big Question {.role-slide}

How should an annotation model connect recorded responses to the linguistic quantity they are intended to measure?

## Answer {.role-slide .compact}

1. Separate recorded responses from the linguistic target.
2. Begin with the instrument and its data-generating process.
3. Assign one probability factor to every random step.
4. Identify item and annotator coordinates before interpretation.
5. Represent gates as part of the observation process.
6. Require parameter recovery before fitting the intended data.

## Question {.role-slide}

Which recorded event licenses every likelihood term, and which model assumption connects that event to the proposed linguistic quantity?
